title: Chronbench: An Incremental HDL Benchmark Suite
problem: FPGA CAD tools compile entire designs from scratch, causing slow development iterations and limiting designer productivity. There is a lack of benchmarks encapsulating realistic HDL development histories, preventing research into sophisticated incremental compilation flows.
motivation: Incremental HDL compilation can significantly accelerate development cycles by reusing previous compilation results, but benchmarks are needed to enable academic research in this area.
method: Chronbench captures realistic HDL development as chronological, synthesizable commits in git repositories. The authors provide a tool to convert public repositories into benchmarks and fully characterize them by synthesizing, placing, and routing 170 commits to analyze development patterns, change magnitudes, and reuse potential.
key_novelty: Encoding realistic HDL development histories as benchmark suites with chronological synthesizable commits in git repositories enables systematic research into incremental compilation.
contributions: Chronbench suite with five benchmarks encapsulating realistic HDL development histories
Automated tool for converting public repositories into Chronbench benchmarks
Full characterization of 170 commits showing realistic development patterns and device utilization changes
Observation that approximately 50% of commits do not significantly impact device utilization, indicating substantial reuse potential

metrics.speedup: incremental compilation potential (characterized but not quantified)

limitations: The paper does not demonstrate actual runtime speedup improvements that incremental compilation could achieve.
